> *This was generated by AI during triage.*

Reviewed at 174861d2. The fix works for the case in #1881. One edge needs a small change before this can merge.

**What I checked.** I ran the built CLI in an isolated home against a local bare team repo, with `init <url> --provider git --agent claude --force`. The baseline is this PR's merge-base, 84561fb0.

| Team repo | Merge-base | This head |
|---|---|---|
| invalid `teamai.yaml` (the issue's), project scope | exit 0; the skeleton is pushed over the team's file | exit 1, `Invalid teamai.yaml: …` and the refusal; origin unchanged |
| same, user scope | exit 0; skeleton pushed | exit 1; origin unchanged |
| self mode | exit 1; an empty `projects/<slug>` left behind | exit 1; nothing left |
| no `teamai.yaml` | exit 0; skeleton | exit 0; skeleton (unchanged) |
| **0-byte `teamai.yaml`** | exit 0; treated as missing, skeleton pushed | **exit 1**, see below |

CI is green at this head.

**[P1 blocking] An empty `teamai.yaml` is now refused, with advice that points at nothing.** `loadTeamConfig` returns null without logging an error when the file has no content (`config.ts:312-316`). The same happens for a file `readRegularFile` refuses, such as a symlink. But `pathExists` is still true for those files, so the new check at `init.ts:2597` refuses them. With a 0-byte `teamai.yaml`, the only error line is:

```
✖ https://git.example.invalid/team/repo.git has a teamai.yaml that does not validate, so init stops instead of replacing it. Fix teamai.yaml in the team repo as the error above says, then run init again.
```

No error is printed above it. Main initializes the same repo and loses nothing, because the file was empty. Either of these fixes it:
- refuse only when the file has content: `const teamYaml = await readFileSafe(path.join(localPath, 'teamai.yaml')); if (!teamConfig && teamYaml?.trim()) …`;
- or keep the refusal and name the cause, as `throwTeamConfigMissingOrInvalid` already does ("it is empty", "the file could not be opened", `config.ts:913-927`).

An empty-file row in the new E2E would pin it.

**[P2 non-blocking]** The new 244-line E2E file builds its own `member` and `bareRepo` helpers. `init-self-mode-refusal.test.ts` already runs the fresh-clone self-mode refusal ("removes newly created clone and writes no local config"), so the two self-mode cases would fit there as one more assertion and a pre-existing-folder case. AGENTS.md asks to extend before adding. Your reason for not using `init-invalid-config-1500.test.ts` (it's about the local config) is fair for the invalid-yaml cases.

**[P3 nit]** After a refusal, an empty `~/.teamai/projects/` and `~/.teamai/debug.log` stay. #1881 asks for the machine to be left as init found it. `debug.log` is probably fine to keep.

**Not this PR, for the record.** The other exits after the clone (`init.ts:2607`, `:2622`, `:2667`, `:2683`, `:2695`) don't go through `refuseInit`, so they still leave the clone and data folder behind. That's from reading the code; I didn't run them. Also, `init --force` from team A to an invalid team B leaves no install, since A's config is moved aside and A's clone removed. Re-running A's init restores it, and the self-mode refusal behaved the same before this PR.

**CI review.** No findings. We disagree: its "no findings" misses the empty-file case above, which I reproduced. We agree the body's real-CLI record is a run at this head.

**Merge risk.** Medium as it stands. The change is one init branch after the clone, before any tool is written. It stops the skeleton overwrite, which is the point, but it also turns an empty `teamai.yaml` from exit 0 into exit 1 with a misleading message.
